Key features: leaf part, pale/light-colored irregular patches, small dark specks, upper leaf surface appearance.

Top candidates: Downy mildew (light green spots on upper surface), Powdery Mildew (white powdery patches), Frogeye leaf spot (gray with reddish-brown borders), Bacterial_Blight (angular water-soaked spots).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
Downy mildew shows discrete yellow spots — test image has larger irregular pale patches. Let me check Powdery Mildew.
Powdery mildew shows white circular powdery patches. The test image has lighter translucent green patches with dark specks — not matching well. Let me check Frogeye and Bean Pod Mottle virus.
Not frogeye — those are distinct circular lesions with defined borders. Let me check Bean Pod Mottle virus and Soybean Vein Necrosis.
Let me check Downy mildew underside view and Soybean Vein Necrosis virus.
Downy mildew shows yellow-green discrete spots. Let me check Soybean Vein Necrosis and Phyllosticta.
Not vein necrosis. I've used 6 views (including test). Let me check Phyllosticta and one more Powdery Mildew view.
Not Phyllosticta. Last view — checking Powdery Mildew for final comparison.

This second Powdery Mildew reference is a strong match. It shows:
- Pale/whitish irregular patches on the leaf surface
- Small dark specks (cleistothecia) scattered throughout
- Exactly the same pattern as the test image

The test image shows a close-up of a leaf with pale irregular patches and dark specks — classic powdery mildew with cleistothecia (small black fruiting bodies). The first powdery mildew reference showed early distinct patches, and this second one shows the exact close-up pattern matching the test image.
